tecnicas.observacao: Pacote de quatro etapas: recuperação de exemplos por BM25 (exemplos resolvidos e código-alvo com localização do erro → exemplos e contexto), análise de causas e geração de plano com 'Forest of Thinking' (várias árvores com CoT e seleção top-n por frequência/self-consistency → raciocinio, decomposicao, amostragem) e geração do patch com CoT; o template de prompt não é reproduzido (instrucao). Comparado com CoT, que usa o mesmo módulo de recuperação (p. 6: 'the retrieval module is consistently used across all control groups'); por isso exemplos e contexto não são contados como acrescentados. O ganho sobre CoT é do pacote, não de um mecanismo isolado. Pacote apenas de prompting, salvo a temperatura 0,7 comum a todas as condições (decodificação, fora do escopo).

citacoes.trecho: This study systematically evaluates the performance of several common CoT techniques in APR tasks and proposes an innovative framework T3, which integrates the powerful reasoning capabilities of LLMs with tree search, effectively improving the precision of generating candidate repair solutions.
T3 decomposes the reasoning process for generating candidate patches into four stages: sample retrieval, cause analysis, repair plan generation, and patch generation.
The top-n results, selected based on cross-tree consistency and voting mechanisms, are then used for further processing.

This paper introduces a novel repair method that achieves substantial improvements over previous approaches; specifically, it improves repair accuracy by 11.20% and 9.90% compared to methods based on CoT reasoning.
These limitations hinder the generation of innovative solutions, increase the risk of entering infinite feedback loops, and ultimately constrain further advancements in repair efficiency.
Custom prompt templates based on four common CoT variants were designed, and experiments were conducted to comparatively analyze their effectiveness in this domain.
“Analogical Reasoning” [14] encourages the generation of examples analogous to the original problem, solving these examples first to inform the final solution.
To retrieve code examples similar to the target program snippet Ptarget, we employ the BM25 algorithm.
To improve the reliability of error cause selection, we introduce a self-consistency mechanism.
Unlike prior work [31], which applies self-consistency for patch selection, we leverage this mechanism to filter and rank error causes.

To ensure the reliability of our results, each program in every experimental group is tested with 30 generated samples, and the temperature parameter is set to 0.7 to mitigate the influence of randomness.

Given that previous experiments conducted by Toufique Ahmed [31] were based on the deprecated code-davinci-002 model, we uniformly select the widely used gpt-3.5-turbo and gpt-4o-mini to eliminate the impact of foundational model discrepancies on repair performance.
To ensure reproducibility, we use the version gpt-3.5-turbo-0125 and gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18

Additionally, we compare our approach with several advanced techniques, including CoT [28], Tree-of-Thought prompt [12], Plan-and-Solve [13], and Analogical Reasoning [14], to provide a comprehensive evaluation.
Specifically, the data for S-C and S-C+BM25 are sourced from [31], while the data for NatGen are obtained from [33].
In contrast, Analogical Reasoning shows markedly lower performance (31.40% on B2Fs, 15.70% on B2Fm), likely due to its dependence on potentially mismatched example retrievals.
This implies that, for complex tasks, the T3 model employs a variety of reasoning pathways to augment overall repair efficacy, notwithstanding a compromise in consistency during patch generation.
Since the retrieval module is consistently used across all control groups, we do not perform ablation on it.
CoT performs even less satisfactorily, as it not only fails to fix the primary error but also modifies correct parts of the target program.
Both methods generate repair patches in a single step, sometimes resolving the issue but often introducing unnecessary modifications to unrelated parts of the program.
